subject: MPA accordion proposal + closure sprint to absorb procurement lag
messages:

To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: HealthCo Procurement <procurement@healthco.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Need to push close by ~3 weeks — procurement notice attached

Karthik,

Quick heads up: procurement just flagged a vendor review that will push our internal approval for the Redwood contract out by ~3 weeks. I attached their notice — it's a standard vendor diligence addendum that they queue into the quarter-end review.

We still want to move forward, but the current MAP dates are now unrealistic. Two asks: (1) can we sketch an interim acceptance approach so we can start staging (canary traffic) while procurement completes? (2) are you able to extend the MPA milestone window and hold pricing/credits as-is while procurement completes?

We appreciate the flexibility. Oliver

Thanks, Oliver — appreciate the heads-up and the PDF.

High-level response: yes, we can do a short-term MPA "accordion" that preserves committed pricing and acceptance conditions but staggers full acceptance into two checkpoints: (A) a canary release window (limited volume; production telemetry) we run immediately once we have signed SOW/annex to the MPA, and (B) formal acceptance after your procurement sign-off (final pull-through). That should let you start integration and reduce risk on your side without us eating indefinite exposure.

I looped in Ben (CS) to confirm the canary playbook and Laura (Finance) to confirm we can hold pricing/credits while procurement finishes. Ben — can you outline what a 2-week closure sprint + canary looks like operationally? Laura — what constraints do we have on preserving credit terms while shifting MAP windows?

I'll assemble a short-facing note and update the MPA draft (MPA_v2_HealthCo.pdf) and send it for a quick sign so you can begin the staging work.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

+1 on the accordion approach. Operational notes:

- Canary scope: 10-20% traffic routing to a dedicated inference pool with telemetry hooks (latency/cost/quality). Duration: 7–10 days.
- Acceptance gates for canary: 95th pctl latency within SLA, errors <0.5%, token-cost delta <5% vs expectation.
- Closure sprint: 2-week focused run to finish integration tasks, test harness, and cutover checklist. We'll provide a daily 15-min stand and a Friday scoreboard.
- Rollback plan: auto-fallback to hosted model variants if anomalies hit gates; we'll keep a hot standby route.

I'll draft the canary runbook and drop it into the MPA addendum. If procurement needs a technical artifact (hosted telemetry SLA), let me know and I can produce a short PDF.

Ben
Ben Carter

Redwood Inference

Thanks all — from Finance perspective here's what we can commit to:

- Pricing protection: we can hold the quoted price for 30 days from the original MPA signature date while procurement completes their additional review. After that window we need to revisit pricing (market/compute costs disclaimers).
- Credits: we cannot apply ad-hoc credits outside of a signed amendment. Proposed alternative: milestone-based credit escrow. If HealthCo signs the MPA addendum (MPA_v2) and triggers the canary, we escrow a small milestone credit that only applies if final acceptance is delayed beyond the agreed final acceptance date. This preserves Redwood's risk posture while giving HealthCo financial downside protection.

I can draft the amendment language today. Two asks for Oliver: (1) confirm who signs for procurement (name + role + email) so we can prepare DocuSign, (2) confirm the internal target for final acceptance once procurement clears (your best estimate).

Laura Bennett
VP, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
